category: Ray Optics: Geometrical Optics interface features, ray releases, optical components, accumulators and ray variables
description: Nodes of the Ray Optics Module's Geometrical Optics (gop) interface - interface settings, medium and ray properties, refraction/reflection and coatings, walls, mirrors and ideal lenses, all ray release features (grid, boundary, point, data file, IES photometric, Gaussian beam, illuminated surface, sun, blackbody, electric field, far-field pattern), scattering, gratings, polarization optics, fluence/deposited power, accumulators, detectors and the built-in ray variables and nonlocal couplings. Type strings and property names are from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models, with a few from the Ray Optics plugin where no model uses the feature.

tools.name: Geometrical Optics: Interface Settings (intensity computation, secondary rays, additional variables)
tools.description: Settings of the Geometrical Optics node that decide which quantities are traced with each ray: monochromatic or polychromatic rays (vacuum wavelength or frequency per ray), the number of preallocated secondary rays for reflected and diffracted rays, the intensity computation (none, intensity, power, both, and graded-media variants) with optional phase and strong-absorption corrections, optical path length, reflection count and ray-status data. It also sets the refractive index of the void and unmeshed domains (absolute vacuum, a given index, or Edlen 1953 air at a temperature and pressure) and which default plots (spot diagram, geometric MTF) are created.
tools.usage: Model Builder > Geometrical Optics (gop) > Settings. API: physics("gop").prop("IntensityComputation").set("IntensityComputation", "ComputeIntensityAndPower"); prop("WavelengthDistribution").setIndex("WavelengthDistribution", "PolychromaticWavelength", 0); prop("MaximumSecondary").setIndex("MaximumSecondary", "500", 0); prop("ComputeOpticalPathLength").setIndex("ComputeOpticalPathLength", true, 0); prop("ExteriorUnmeshedProperties").setIndex("DispersionModel", "AirEdlen1953", 0)

parameters.name: WavelengthDistribution
parameters.description: Monochromatic (default), PolychromaticWavelength (specify vacuum wavelength) or polychromatic by frequency.

parameters.name: MaximumSecondary
parameters.description: Preallocated secondary rays for reflections at material discontinuities and grating orders; total internal reflection needs none.

parameters.name: IntensityComputation
parameters.description: NoneIntensityComputation (default), ComputeIntensity, ComputePower, ComputeIntensityAndPower, and 'in graded media' variants; ComputePhase and 'Use corrections for strongly absorbing media' checkboxes.

parameters.name: Additional variables
parameters.description: ComputeOpticalPathLength (gop.L), CountReflections (gop.Nrefl), StoreRayStatusData (gop.rti, gop.st, gop.fs), OnlyStoreAccumulatedVariables.

parameters.name: ExteriorUnmeshedProperties
parameters.description: DispersionModel AbsoluteVacuum | SpecifyRefractiveIndex (next, kiext) | AirEdlen1953 (Text, Pext).

parameters.name: UseGeometryNormals / Results / advanced
parameters.description: Geometry vs mesh normals; default plots; wall accuracy order, random-number arguments, multiple release times, maximum wall interactions per step (1000).

tools.notes: Every option adds degrees of freedom per ray; Only store accumulated variables keeps files small when only fluence or heat sources are needed. Setting MaximumSecondary to 0 hides reflected rays in imaging systems, but a stray-light analysis needs secondary rays. The Geometrical Optics interface itself is catalogued as 'Geometrical Optics (gop)'.

tools.name: Ray Properties (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Default global node of the Geometrical Optics interface that defines the ray equations and, for monochromatic models, the common ray vacuum wavelength or frequency. Only one instance exists; in polychromatic models the wavelength or frequency is instead set by each release feature.
tools.usage: Geometrical Optics > Ray Properties 1 (default, tag op1). API: physics("gop").feature("op1").set("RayPropertySpecification", "SpecifyVacuumWavelength"); feature("op1").set("lambda0", "550[nm]")

parameters.name: RayPropertySpecification
parameters.description: SpecifyVacuumWavelength (default) or SpecifyFrequency.

parameters.name: lambda0 / nu
parameters.description: Vacuum wavelength (default 660 nm) or frequency (default 4.54e14 Hz).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gop").feature("op1").set("lambda0", "248[nm]");
// UV reactor at 248 nm: Ray_Optics_Module/Ultraviolet_Sterilization/annular_ultraviolet_reactor
tools.notes: Dispersion models in Medium Properties are evaluated at this wavelength (or at each ray's own wavelength in polychromatic mode).

tools.name: Medium Properties (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Default domain node that sets the refractive index of the traced media: an absolute index, a relative index (to air at a reference temperature and pressure), an index and Abbe number with a Cauchy/Conrady/linear model, a dispersion model picked from a list, or 'Get dispersion model from material', which detects each glass's model from the Optical Material Library automatically. When intensity or power is computed it also sets absorption through the extinction coefficient, attenuation coefficient or internal transmittance at 2/5/10/25 mm, and an optional Schott thermo-optic offset.
tools.usage: Geometrical Optics > Medium Properties 1 (default, tag mp1). API: physics("gop").feature("mp1").set("n_mat", "userdef"); set("n", new String[]{"1.5084", "0", "0", "0", "1.5084", "0", "0", "0", "1.5084"}); set("ki_mat", "from_mat")

parameters.name: Refractive index of domains
parameters.description: Specify absolute refractive index (default), Specify relative refractive index, Specify relative refractive index and Abbe number, Get dispersion model from list, Get dispersion model from material.

parameters.name: n / ki (n_mat, ki_mat)
parameters.description: Real index and imaginary part, From material or User defined.

parameters.name: Optical attenuation model
parameters.description: Extinction coefficient, Attenuation coefficient (1/m), Internal transmittance at 2, 5, 10 or 25 mm; converted automatically between forms.

parameters.name: Thermo-optic dispersion model
parameters.description: None or Schott thermo-optic (coefficients and reference temperature From material); disabled for Temperature-dependent Sellmeier.

tools.example:
Petzval lens with catalog glasses: Medium Properties 1 > Refractive index of domains = Get dispersion model from material; Temperature = 20[degC]; release polychromatic rays and compare spot sizes per wavelength.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/petzval_lens, double_gauss_lens
tools.notes: The domain variable is gop.nref_local (ray variable gop.nref); built-in gop.nrefd/nrefF/nrefC and the Abbe number gop.Vd are handy for plotting dispersive media. Unmeshed domains and the void use the interface's exterior index.

tools.name: Optical Dispersion and Thermo-Optic Models (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Built-in refractive-index formulas of the Ray Optics Module: Cauchy, Conrady, Herzberger, Schott, Schott extended, Sellmeier, Sellmeier modified type 1 and type 2, and Temperature-dependent Sellmeier (absolute index versus wavelength and temperature), plus the Edlen (1953) model of air used for exterior domains and for converting catalog indices relative to air into absolute indices. A Schott thermo-optic model adds a temperature-dependent index offset to any model except the temperature-dependent Sellmeier.
tools.usage: Medium Properties > Refractive index of domains = Get dispersion model from list (choose the model, enter coefficients) or Get dispersion model from material; material data appear as material models such as DispersionModelSellmeierStandard, DispersionModelCauchy, InternalTransmittance10, ThermoOpticDispersionModelSchott.

parameters.name: Coefficients
parameters.description: Wavelength always in micrometers inside the formulas (e.g. Schott A0, A1 [um^2]...); stored as gop.ODsma1.. for Sellmeier.

parameters.name: Reference temperature / pressure
parameters.description: Conditions of the air relative to which the catalog index was measured; set pressure 0 to treat the index as absolute.

parameters.name: Thermo-optic coefficients
parameters.description: Schott D0, D1, D2, E0, E1, lambda_TK with a reference temperature.

tools.example:
Plot the d-line index of all lenses: Slice/Volume plot of gop.nrefd, or at any wavelength subst(gop.nref_local, gop.mp1.lambda0, 587.56[nm]).
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/double_gauss_lens (Sellmeier + Schott thermo-optic from the material library)
tools.notes: Evaluating gop.nref_local directly in a Slice plot fails for dispersive media because it depends on the ray wavelength (noenv construction); use gop.nrefd/nrefF/nrefC or subst().

tools.name: Material Discontinuity (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Default boundary node that refracts rays by Snell's law at every boundary between media of different index and, using preallocated secondary rays, releases the reflected ray; with intensity or power computed, both are weighted by the polarization-dependent Fresnel equations. Its Coatings section models antireflective coatings, single layers, stacks of Thin Dielectric Film subnodes (optionally repeated N times, e.g. Bragg mirrors) or directly specified reflectance/transmittance; the Rays to Release section can suppress reflected rays always, never, by expression or below an intensity/power threshold.
tools.usage: Geometrical Optics > Material Discontinuity 1 (default on all boundaries) or add more with specific coatings. API: physics("gop").create("matd2", "MaterialDiscontinuity", 2); feature("matd2").set("ThinDielectricFilmsOnBoundary", "AddLayersToSurface"); set("ReleaseReflectedRays", "Never")

parameters.name: ThinDielectricFilmsOnBoundary
parameters.description: NoneLayer (default), AddLayersToSurface, AddLayersToSurfaceRepeating (Nft unit cells), Antireflective coating, Single-layer coating (nf, tf), Specify reflectance (Rf), Specify transmittance (Tr); s/p values optional.

parameters.name: Treat as single layer dielectric film
parameters.description: Derive one layer that gives the specified R/T at a given wavelength and angle.

parameters.name: ReleaseReflectedRays / Ith / Qth / e
parameters.description: Always (default), Never, or Based on logical expression; thresholds 1 mW/m^2 and 1e-3 mW.

parameters.name: Reset optical path length / Show boundary normal
parameters.description: Advanced settings.

tools.notes: If all secondary rays are used up, reflected rays are silently dropped and the solver issues a warning; increase Maximum number of secondary rays. An Accumulator (Boundary) subnode can count hits.

tools.name: Thin Dielectric Film (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Subnode of Material Discontinuity or Wall that adds one thin, transparent dielectric layer (refractive index and thickness) to the surface, modifying the Fresnel coefficients used for reflected and refracted ray intensity, power, phase and polarization. Several subnodes are stacked in Model Builder order from the upside to the downside of the boundary, and with the repeating option selected layers form a periodic unit cell.
tools.usage: Right-click Material Discontinuity / Wall (with Coatings = Add layers to surface) > Thin Dielectric Film. API: physics("gop").feature("matd2").create("film1", "ThinDielectricFilm", 2); feature("matd2").feature("film1").set("nf", "n_CeF3"); set("tf", "lam0/(4*n_CeF3)")

parameters.name: nf
parameters.description: Film refractive index (default 1).

parameters.name: tf
parameters.description: Film thickness (default 1 um), small compared with the coherence length.

parameters.name: RepeatLayerInMultilayerFilms
parameters.description: Include the layer in the repeating unit cell.

tools.example:
Quarter-wave AR stack: film1 nf = n_CeF3, tf = lam0/(4*n_CeF3); film2 nf = n_ZrO2, tf = lam0/(2*n_ZrO2).
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Prisms_and_Coatings/achromatic_phase_shifter
tools.notes: Requires intensity or power computation. Check the boundary normal (Show boundary normal) because layer order depends on it.

tools.name: Wall (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Boundary condition of the Geometrical Optics interface that decides what rays do on contact: Freeze (default, keep final position and direction - typical for detectors), Specular reflection, Stick, Disappear, Pass through, Diffuse scattering (Lambertian), Isotropic scattering, Mixed diffuse and specular, or General reflection with a user direction; a Primary ray condition applies the wall condition only with a probability or when an expression is true, with an 'Otherwise' condition for the rest. With intensity/power computed it adds absorption/reflection/transmission coefficients (s/p separately), Rayleigh surface roughness for specular walls, wavelength/frequency reinitialization and subnodes for coatings, accumulators and deposited ray power.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Wall. API: physics("gop").create("wall1", "Wall", 2); feature("wall1").set("WallCondition", "Freeze"); feature("wall1").set("PrimaryRayCondition", "Expression"); set("e", "gop.Nrefl>0"); set("Otherwise", "Pass")

parameters.name: WallCondition
parameters.description: Freeze, SpecularReflection, Disappear, Pass, DiffuseScattering (verified values) plus Stick, Isotropic scattering, Mixed diffuse and specular reflection, General reflection (Lprim).

parameters.name: PrimaryRayCondition / gamma / e / Otherwise
parameters.description: NoneCondition, Probability (gamma) or Expression; alternative condition for the remaining rays.

parameters.name: ComputeReflectedIntensityUsing
parameters.description: AbsorptionCoefficients (alpha, t) or reflection coefficients (R, t); s/p specific values optional.

parameters.name: SurfaceRoughnessModel / sigmar
parameters.description: None or Rayleigh roughness (RMS roughness).

parameters.name: ReinitializeWavelength / ReinitializeFrequency
parameters.description: Resample the ray wavelength or frequency (None, Normal, Lognormal, Uniform) at the wall.

tools.notes: Pass through does not refract; use Material Discontinuity for refraction. Random-number based conditions depend on the interface's random-argument setting; test statistical convergence with more rays. The generic particle/ray wall is catalogued as 'Wall (rays)'.

tools.name: Mirror (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Convenience boundary condition that always reflects rays specularly, with the Wall's absorption/reflection coefficient settings, optional Rayleigh surface roughness, wavelength or frequency reinitialization and auxiliary-variable updates. Use it for flat, spherical, parabolic and off-axis mirrors in telescopes, laser cavities and concentrators.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Mirror. API: physics("gop").create("mir1", "Mirror", 2); feature("mir1").set("ComputeReflectedIntensityUsing", "AbsorptionCoefficients"); set("alpha", "0.02")

parameters.name: ComputeReflectedIntensityUsing / alpha / R / t
parameters.description: Absorption or reflection coefficients, s/p specific optional.

parameters.name: SurfaceRoughnessModel / sigmar
parameters.description: Rayleigh roughness reduces specular intensity by exp(-(2*k*sigma*cos(theta))^2).

parameters.name: Reset optical path length
parameters.description: Advanced setting.

tools.notes: Equivalent to a Wall with Specular reflection. Rayleigh roughness applies when sigma < lambda/(8*cos(theta_i)).

tools.name: Ideal Lens (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Boundary condition that makes a flat surface (3D) or straight edge (2D) act as a lens without modeling its geometry: a paraxial surface with a given effective focal length or optical power, a thin lens from two radii of curvature and an index, or a thick lens that also has a center thickness. Rays through the lens pole are undeviated. It is ideal for early system layout, cavity design and replacing well-corrected sub-systems.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Ideal Lens (one node per lens). Type string: IdealLens.

parameters.name: Ideal lens type
parameters.description: Paraxial surface (default; effective focal length 100 mm or optical power 0.1 1/m), Thin lens (R1, R2 = 100 mm, n = 1.5), Thick lens (plus center thickness Tc).

parameters.name: Ideal lens reference
parameters.description: Centroid of selection, From coordinates (projected onto the lens plane) or Selected point.

tools.example: Early layout of a two-lens relay: draw two flat disks where the lenses will sit, apply Ideal Lens 1 (Paraxial surface, effective focal length 100 mm) and Ideal Lens 2 (Thin lens, R1 = 50 mm, R2 = -50 mm, n = 1.45), release a collimated Release from Grid bundle and check the image position with a Spot Diagram before replacing them with real lens geometry.
tools.notes: A lens without aberrations; for aberration studies model the real surfaces (e.g. from the Ray Optics Part Library).

tools.name: Release (Geometrical Optics, domain release)
tools.description: Ray release feature for domains that places rays either with a number density proportional to an expression (N rays per release) or at mesh-based positions (element centers of a refined mesh), then assigns directions (expression, spherical, hemispherical, conical, Lambertian), wavelength or frequency distributions, initial phase, intensity or source power, wavefront curvature and polarization. It is the base from which the other release features inherit most sections.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Release. Type string: Release. Common sections: Release Times, Initial Position, Ray Direction Vector, Initial Ray Frequency / Vacuum Wavelength, Initial Phase, Initial Intensity, Initial Radii of Curvature, Initial Polarization, Total Source Power.

parameters.name: Initial position
parameters.description: Density (Number of rays per release N = 100, Density proportional to rho, accuracy order, position refinement factor) or Mesh based (refinement factor 1-5).

parameters.name: Ray direction vector
parameters.description: Expression (L0), Spherical, Hemispherical, Conical, Lambertian (3D) with Nw rays in wave vector space (default 50).

parameters.name: Initial intensity / Total source power
parameters.description: I0 = 1000 W/m^2 for single rays; Psrc = 1 W (or W/m in 2D) distributed uniformly or by a weighting factor Pwt.

parameters.name: Initial polarization
parameters.description: Unpolarized (default), Fully or Partially polarized with amplitudes, phase difference and degree of polarization.

parameters.name: Wavefront shape
parameters.description: Plane wave (default), Spherical/Cylindrical wave (r0) or Ellipsoid.

tools.example: Fluorescent volume source: Release on the dye domain with Density proportional to c_dye, N = 5000, Ray direction vector = Spherical (Nw = 20, Random sampling), Total source power 10 mW.
tools.notes: Positions are based on the mesh, so they change slightly with the mesh or geometry kernel. The density expression must be strictly positive.

tools.name: Release from Boundary (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Releases rays from surfaces (3D) or edges (2D): positions on a projected plane grid (3D default), uniform distribution (2D default), density or mesh based, and directions given in global or local tangential/normal coordinates (Expression, Hemispherical, Conical, Lambertian). In 3D the initial wavefront can follow the surface curvature, which makes it ideal for emitting surfaces such as LEDs, lamp envelopes and image objects; a Nonlocal Accumulator subnode can report what the rays from each emitting element later hit.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Release from Boundary. API: physics("gop").create("relb1", "ReleaseFromBoundary", 2); feature("relb1").set("InitialPosition", "Density"); set("Nr", "100000"); set("dpro", "comp1.im1(x,y)"); set("RayDirectionVector", "Conical")

parameters.name: InitialPosition / Nr / dpro
parameters.description: Projected plane grid, Uniform distribution, Density (Nr rays, density expression dpro) or Mesh based.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector / SpecifyInletTangentialNormal
parameters.description: Expression, Hemispherical, Conical or Lambertian; directions in (t1, t2, n) if selected.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Global or any defined system for the direction components.

parameters.name: Wavefront shape (3D)
parameters.description: From surface curvature (default), Plane, Spherical or Ellipsoid.

tools.example:
Image simulation: Release from Boundary on the object plane with Density proportional to an Image function (dpro = comp1.im1(x,y)), Nr = 100000, Conical directions toward the entrance pupil; the Spot Diagram at the image plane reproduces the picture.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/double_gauss_lens_image_simulation
tools.notes: The normal used for releases may be opposite to the geometric normal so that positive normal components point into the domain.

tools.name: Release from Edge and Release from Point (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Release from Edge emits rays from positions along selected 3D edges (density, uniform or mesh based), and Release from Point emits from selected geometry points - one ray per point, or many when the direction (e.g. a conical or hexapolar cone for a point object at a given numerical aperture) or wavelength is sampled from a distribution. Point releases are the usual way to model object points or field points of an imaging system.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Edges > Release from Edge; Points > Release from Point. API: physics("gop").create("rpt1", "ReleaseFromPoint", 0); feature("rpt1").set("RayDirectionVector", "Conical"); set("ConicalDistribution", "Hexapolar"); set("alphac", "atan(NA)"); physics("gop").create("rele1", "ReleaseFromEdge", 1)

parameters.name: Initial position (edge)
parameters.description: Density (default), Uniform distribution (N segments) or Mesh based.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector / Nw / cax / alphac
parameters.description: Direction distribution, number of rays, cone axis and angle.

parameters.name: Wavelength distribution (polychromatic)
parameters.description: E.g. List of values lambda0vals for several spectral lines.

tools.notes: Points must be geometry vertices; for arbitrary locations use Release from Grid.

tools.name: Release from Symmetry Axis, Point on Axis and Grid on Axis (Geometrical Optics, 2D axisymmetric)
tools.description: Release features restricted to the symmetry axis of 2D axisymmetric models: Release from Symmetry Axis (edges on the axis, uniform/mesh/density positions; Expression, Spherical - weighted toward the radial direction to mimic equal solid angles in 3D - or Conical directions), Release from Point on Axis and Release from Grid on Axis (grid of z positions with r = 0). They let on-axis sources of rotationally symmetric optics be modeled at 2D cost.
tools.usage: 2D axisymmetric component > Physics toolbar > Release from Symmetry Axis / Release from Point on Axis / Release from Grid on Axis. Type strings: ReleaseFromSymmetryAxis, ReleaseFromPointOnAxis, ReleaseGridOnAxis.

parameters.name: Initial position (symmetry axis)
parameters.description: Uniform distribution (N = 100), Mesh based or Density.

parameters.name: Ray direction vector
parameters.description: Expression (radial and axial components), Spherical or Conical.

parameters.name: Initial coordinates (grid on axis)
parameters.description: List of z positions.

tools.example: Axisymmetric reflector lamp: Release from Point on Axis at the filament with Spherical directions (Nw = 200) and Mirror on the paraboloid; compare with the 3D model for validation.
tools.notes: Add Walls on axis segments without geometry, otherwise rays can wander into r < 0.

tools.name: Release from Grid: Cylindrical and Hexapolar Grids (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Geometrical Optics' Release from Grid (Java type ReleaseGrid) places rays at user-defined grid points anywhere, even outside the geometry: All combinations or Specified combinations of coordinate lists, or - in 3D - Cylindrical grids (uniform radius intervals, uniform number density or user radii, with N_phi angles plus a center ray) and Hexapolar grids (rings of 6, 12, 18 ... points), which are the standard way to fill an entrance pupil with a collimated beam at several field angles. Preview buttons show the grid points and extents.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Release from Grid. API: physics("gop").create("relg1", "ReleaseGrid", -1); feature("relg1").set("GridType", "Hexapolar"); set("qcc", new String[]{"0", "0", "-1[m]"}); set("rcc", new String[]{"0", "0", "1"}); set("Rc", "D_pupil/2"); set("Ncr", "10"); set("L0", new String[]{"sin(th)", "0", "cos(th)"})

parameters.name: GridType
parameters.description: AllCombinations (default), Specified combinations, Cylindrical (3D), Hexapolar (3D).

parameters.name: x0 (qx0, qy0, qz0)
parameters.description: Coordinate lists for rectangular/arbitrary grids.

parameters.name: qcc / rcc / Rc / Ncr / Nphi / RadialDistribution
parameters.description: Center, axis, radius, number of radial positions (default 5), angles (default 10), UniformRadiusIntervals or uniform density.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector / L0
parameters.description: Expression for collimated beams or cone distributions.

tools.notes: Hexapolar grids have 3*Nc*(Nc+1)+1 points. The generic particle/ray 'Release from Grid' entry lists a different type string; for Geometrical Optics the recorded type is ReleaseGrid.

tools.name: Conical, Hexapolar and Lambertian Ray Direction Distributions (Geometrical Optics releases)
tools.description: Direction options shared by the ray release features: a single Expression direction, Spherical, Hemispherical, Conical (cone axis and half-angle) or Lambertian (3D, cosine-weighted hemisphere) distributions with Nw rays, sampled deterministically (reproducible, evenly spread) or randomly. For cones, 3D offers Uniform density, Specify polar and azimuthal distributions (N_theta x N_phi + 1 rays), Hexapolar (3*N_theta*(N_theta+1)+1 rays), Flat fans, Marginal rays only and Marginal and axial rays - the last ones useful for paraxial checks and ray-fan plots.
tools.usage: Any release feature > Ray Direction Vector. API: feature("relg1").set("RayDirectionVector", "Conical"); set("ConicalDistribution", "Hexapolar"); set("Nctheta", "10"); set("cax", new String[]{"0", "0", "1"}); set("alphac", "asin(NA)"); set("SamplingFromDistribution", "Deterministic")

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: Expression (default), Spherical, Hemispherical, Conical, Lambertian.

parameters.name: ConicalDistribution
parameters.description: UniformDensity (default), polar/azimuthal, Hexapolar, Flat, Marginal rays only, Marginal and axial rays.

parameters.name: Nw / Nctheta / Ncphi / cax / alphac / et
parameters.description: Ray count, polar/azimuthal counts, cone axis, cone angle (default pi/3), transverse direction for fans.

parameters.name: SamplingFromDistribution
parameters.description: Deterministic (default) or Random.

tools.example:
Point object at NA 0.2 imaged by a lens: Release from Point with Conical, Hexapolar, Nctheta = 10 (331 directions), alphac = asin(0.2); a Spot Diagram then gives the point spread.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/ray_optics_modeling_fresnel_lens
tools.notes: Total Source Power is distributed over the directions (uniformly or by a weighting factor), or taken from a Photometric Data Import IES file.

tools.name: Polychromatic and Blackbody Wavelength Sampling (Geometrical Optics releases)
tools.description: When the interface is set to polychromatic rays, every release feature gets a Vacuum Wavelength (or Initial Ray Frequency) section that assigns each ray its own wavelength: a single value, Normal, Lognormal or Uniform distributions, a List of values (e.g. the F, d and C spectral lines), or Blackbody sampling by Planck's law at a temperature (default 5780 K) either within a fraction of the total emissive power (default 0.95) or a specified band. This is how chromatic aberration, spectrometer dispersion and solar spectra are traced.
tools.usage: Geometrical Optics > Wavelength distribution of released rays = Polychromatic; release feature > Vacuum Wavelength. API: physics("gop").prop("WavelengthDistribution").setIndex("WavelengthDistribution", "PolychromaticWavelength", 0); feature("relg1").set("LDistributionFunction", "ListOfValues"); set("lambda0vals", "486.1[nm] 587.6[nm] 656.3[nm]")

parameters.name: LDistributionFunction / FDistributionFunction
parameters.description: NoneDistribution (default), Normal, Lognormal, Uniform, Blackbody, ListOfValues (From file for data-file releases).

parameters.name: lambda0 / lambda0mean / lambda0std / lambda0min / lambda0max / lambda0Nval
parameters.description: Parameters (defaults 660 nm, 100 nm std, 400-700 nm).

parameters.name: Tbbl / DistributionType_lambda0 / fbbl
parameters.description: Blackbody temperature, fraction of emissive power or bandwidth.

parameters.name: SamplingFromDistribution_lambda0
parameters.description: Deterministic or Random.

tools.example:
Czerny-Turner monochromator with a list of wavelengths from a Release from Point; rays are colored by gop.lambda0 in the Ray Trajectories plot and grouped per wavelength with a Ray Bin dataset.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Spectrometers_and_Monochromators/czerny_turner_monochromator, Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/gregory_maksutov_telescope
tools.notes: Adds one degree of freedom per ray; the number of values multiplies the number of released rays at each release point.

tools.name: Release from Data File (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Releases rays whose initial positions (and optionally directions, wavelength/frequency and auxiliary variable values) are read from a whitespace-separated text file with one ray per row, with column indices chosen in the settings. The loaded distribution can be scaled, rotated with Z-X-Z Euler angles and translated, which makes it the bridge to measured ray sets or source models exported from other optical software.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Release from Data File; Browse > Import. Type string: ReleaseFromDataFile.

parameters.name: Filename / Index of first column containing position data
parameters.description: Zero-based column index (default 0); lines starting with % are comments.

parameters.name: Transformations
parameters.description: Scale factor R (e.g. 0.001 for mm data), Euler angles (3D) or rotation angle (2D), displacement vector (applied last).

parameters.name: Ray direction vector
parameters.description: Expression, From file (first direction column, default 3, optional 'Rotate initial directions'), or the usual distributions.

parameters.name: Wavelength / frequency / auxiliary values
parameters.description: From file columns or distributions.

tools.example: LED source file with columns x y z Lx Ly Lz lambda (mm, um): Scale factor 0.001, Ray direction vector = From file (index 3), Vacuum Wavelength = From file (index 6, polychromatic interface).
tools.notes: All rows must have the same number of columns.

tools.name: Photometric Data Import (Geometrical Optics, IES files)
tools.description: 3D global node that imports an IESNA LM-63 photometric data file (*.ies) describing a luminaire's intensity versus direction, so release features can initialize ray intensity and power from real lamp data. After import, select the node in a release feature's Total Source Power 'Intensity initialization' list together with a Spherical, Hemispherical, Conical or Lambertian direction distribution, and orient it with the photometric horizontal and zero directions.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Photometric Data Import > Filename > Import; release feature > Total Source Power > Intensity initialization = Photometric Data Import 1. Type string: PhotometricDataImport.

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: IES file (ANSI/IESNA LM-63-02); Import and Discard buttons.

parameters.name: Photometric horizontal ph / Photometric zero pz (release feature)
parameters.description: Orientation vectors, default +x and +z.

tools.example: Street-lamp illuminance on a road: Photometric Data Import of the vendor IES file, Release from Point at the lamp with Spherical directions (Nw = 5000) and Intensity initialization from the IES node; Accumulator (Boundary) on the road sums deposited power per area.
tools.notes: Only TILT=NONE files are supported; requires 3D and intensity computation.

tools.name: Gaussian Beam (Geometrical Optics ray release)
tools.description: Release feature that samples rays from a Gaussian beam with a given waist position and beam axis in either of two asymptotic limits: as a Point source (small Rayleigh range; rays leave the waist in a cone set by the divergence half-angle, waist radius or Rayleigh range) or as a Collimated source (large Rayleigh range; rays start on a grid across the waist). Ray powers follow the Gaussian profile truncated by a cutoff ratio (default 2, i.e. 99.97 % of the power), with circular or elliptical cross-sections and a specified total power, encircled power or peak intensity.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Gaussian Beam (requires intensity or power computation). Type string: GaussianBeam.

parameters.name: Beam waist position qw / Beam axis r
parameters.description: Default origin and +z (3D) or +x (2D); 2D-axi: waist z and axis direction.

parameters.name: Beam type
parameters.description: Point source (default; N_theta polar angles, 3*N_theta*(N_theta+1)+1 rays in 3D) or Collimated source (Nc radial positions).

parameters.name: Beam dimensions
parameters.description: Divergence half-angle (1 mrad), waist radius (1 mm, or HWHM), or Rayleigh range (1 mm).

parameters.name: Beam cutoff ratio c / cross-section shape
parameters.description: Default 2; Circular or Elliptical (aspect ratio, major axis direction).

parameters.name: Intensity specification / Initial polarization
parameters.description: Total beam power, Encircled power or Peak intensity; polarization reference direction and amplitudes.

tools.example: Fiber-coupled laser focused by a lens: Gaussian Beam, Point source, Beam waist radius 5 um at the fiber tip, Total source power 1 W; Deposited Ray Power on the target wall gives the irradiance.
tools.notes: Geometrical optics ignores diffraction, so the ray bundle reproduces the far-field divergence or the near-field profile but not the full beam evolution; use Beam Envelopes/ewfd for diffraction-limited propagation.

tools.name: Illuminated Surface (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Boundary release that emits rays already reflected (or refracted) by a surface lit by an external source - a user-defined direction, a point source or the sun at a location and time - so the first, uninteresting propagation leg is skipped; shadowing by other objects is not considered. Corrections for the finite solar disk (light cones or conical sampling within 4.65 mrad, with limb darkening) and surface slope errors (Rayleigh-distributed normal perturbation) make it the standard source for solar concentrators and glare studies.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Illuminated Surface. API: physics("gop").create("ill1", "IlluminatedSurface", 2); feature("ill1").set("IncidentRayDirectionVector", "SolarRadiation"); set("LocationDefinedBy", "City"); set("FiniteSource", "SampleFromDistribution"); set("IncludeSurfaceRoughness", "1"); set("sigmaphi", "1[mrad]")

parameters.name: RaysToRelease / ReflectionCoefficientCalculation
parameters.description: Reflected (absorption and transmission coefficients or refractive indices) or Refracted (exterior index).

parameters.name: IncidentRayDirectionVector
parameters.description: UserDefinedDirection (Li), User-defined point source (rsrc) or SolarRadiation (location, date, local time).

parameters.name: FiniteSource / psim / LimbDarkeningModel
parameters.description: NoneCorrection, Create light cones at release points, SampleFromDistribution; max disk angle 4.65 mrad; limb darkening None, Empirical power law, Linear, User defined.

parameters.name: IncludeSurfaceRoughness / sigmaphi
parameters.description: Surface slope error (default 1 mrad).

parameters.name: Nr / InitialPosition
parameters.description: Number of rays and position method (as Release from Boundary).

tools.notes: Incident ray intensity defaults to 1000 W/m^2. Because shadowing is ignored, select only surfaces that see the source directly.

tools.name: Solar Radiation (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Global release feature that launches a grid of rays (same grid options as Release from Grid) traveling in the direction of the sun computed from latitude, longitude, time zone, date and local time, or from a list of cities; x, y, z correspond to North, West and up. Solar irradiance, finite-disk corrections and limb darkening are included, and a parametric sweep over time of day gives sun-path studies for heliostats, receivers and glare from buildings.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Solar Radiation. Type string: SolarRadiation.

parameters.name: Location defined by
parameters.description: Coordinates (latitude 36.1, longitude -115.2, time zone -8 by default; enter unitless degrees/hours) or City (with daylight-saving option).

parameters.name: Date / Local time
parameters.description: Day, month, year (valid 2000-2199) and hour, minute, second; values may overflow (e.g. 81 s).

parameters.name: Corrections for finite source diameter / Limb darkening
parameters.description: As in Illuminated Surface (max disk angle 4.65 mrad).

parameters.name: Initial coordinates
parameters.description: Grid settings from Release from Grid.

tools.example: Heliostat field efficiency over a day: Solar Radiation with City, date 21 June, and a Parametric Sweep of the hour parameter 7-19; Accumulator (Boundary) on the receiver collects power.
tools.notes: The sun position is recomputed if inputs change during a study; because ray transit times are tiny, time-of-day variation belongs in a parametric sweep.

tools.name: Blackbody Radiation (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: 3D boundary release that emits rays diffusely (Lambert's cosine law) from one side of hot surfaces, with total power from the Stefan-Boltzmann law at the surface temperature and, in polychromatic models, wavelengths sampled from Planck's law. The temperature can be a value or a temperature field solved by a heat transfer interface, which makes it useful for thermal-emission and stray-radiation studies in infrared systems.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Blackbody Radiation (3D). Type string: BlackbodyRadiation.

parameters.name: Temperature T
parameters.description: Default 293.15 K, or a solved temperature from the list.

parameters.name: Number of rays per release N
parameters.description: Default 1000, randomly distributed over the surfaces.

parameters.name: Reverse direction
parameters.description: Flip the emitting side (normal arrows shown in the Graphics window).

tools.example: Self-emission of a warm lens barrel onto an IR detector: Blackbody Radiation on the barrel's inner surfaces with T from Heat Transfer in Solids, polychromatic 3-14 um rays, Freeze wall with Deposited Ray Power on the detector.
tools.notes: Requires ray intensity or power computation for meaningful powers.

tools.name: Ray Termination (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Single global node that removes rays that leave a bounding box (the geometry's box enlarged by 5 %, a user-defined box, or none) and, when intensity or power is computed, rays whose intensity or power falls below thresholds. Terminating escaped and negligible rays keeps trajectories short and lets the Ray Tracing study stop early with the 'No active rays remaining' or intensity stop conditions.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Ray Termination. API: physics("gop").create("rt1", "RayTermination", -1); feature("rt1").set("SpatialExtentsOfRayPropagation", "BoundingBoxFromGeometry"); set("AdditionalTerminationCriteria", "NoneTerminationCriteria")

parameters.name: SpatialExtentsOfRayPropagation
parameters.description: BoundingBoxFromGeometry (default), Bounding box user defined (xmin..zmax), None.

parameters.name: AdditionalTerminationCriteria / Ith / Qth
parameters.description: None, Intensity, Power, or both; thresholds 1 mW/m^2 and 1e-3 mW.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gop").create("rt1", "RayTermination", -1);
// Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Laser_Cavities/bow_tie_laser_cavity, two_mirror_laser_cavity
tools.notes: Rays released outside the box only disappear after entering and leaving it. Exact termination times are found analytically for planar waves in absorbing media or spherical/ellipsoidal waves in nonabsorbing media.

tools.name: Scattering Domain (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Domain feature for extinction by small spherical particles in a medium (turbid water, aerosols, tissue phantoms): cross sections come from Rayleigh theory, full Mie theory, large conducting spheres, user efficiency factors or user cross sections, with particle radius, number density and complex refractive index. In the Deterministic model ray intensity/power decays continuously; in the Random (Monte Carlo) model rays are extinguished at sampled times and then disappear, freeze or are scattered with a Henyey-Greenstein or Rayleigh phase function, and the dissipated power can be accumulated.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Scattering Domain. Type string: ScatteringDomain.

parameters.name: Scattering model
parameters.description: Deterministic or Random (default) when intensity/power is computed.

parameters.name: Cross section calculation
parameters.description: Small spheres (Rayleigh, default), General spheres (Mie), Large conducting spheres, Specify efficiency factors (Qext, Qsca), Specify cross section.

parameters.name: Rsc / Nsc / np,r / np,i
parameters.description: Particle radius (10 nm), number density (1e20 1/m^3), refractive index (1.4, 1e-6).

parameters.name: Effect on primary ray / phase function
parameters.description: Disappear, Freeze or Scatter (Henyey-Greenstein g = 0.95 or Rayleigh).

parameters.name: Accumulation of dissipated energy
parameters.description: Extinction, Scattering or Absorption.

tools.example: UV disinfection reactor with suspended particles: Scattering Domain (Random, General spheres (Mie), Rsc = 1[um], Nsc = 1e12[1/m^3], Scatter with Henyey-Greenstein g = 0.9) combined with Fluence Rate Calculation.
tools.notes: Monte Carlo results need enough rays for statistical convergence.

tools.name: Scattering Boundary (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Boundary feature that scatters rays in reflection and/or transmission at a surface using diffuse (Lambertian), isotropic or surface-slope-error models, e.g. frosted glass, diffusers, rough lens surfaces and ground-glass screens. It can also reinitialize ray wavelength or frequency (fluorescence-like conversion) and reset the optical path length.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Scattering Boundary. Type string: ScatteringBoundary.

parameters.name: Scattering model
parameters.description: Diffuse scattering, Isotropic scattering or Surface slope error (sigma, default 1 mrad).

parameters.name: Rays to release
parameters.description: Reflected and transmitted (default; primary ray transmitted unless TIR), Reflected, or Transmitted.

parameters.name: Wavelength or frequency reinitialization
parameters.description: None, Normal, Lognormal or Uniform.

tools.example: LED behind a diffuser plate: Scattering Boundary on the exit face with Diffuse scattering, Transmitted rays, then an Accumulator (Boundary) on a target screen to map illuminance uniformity.
tools.notes: Uses random numbers; the random-number argument setting of the interface controls reproducibility.

tools.name: Release from Electric Field (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Multiscale release that starts rays on a boundary with intensity and polarization taken from an electric field computed by a wave-optics or RF frequency-domain interface (or a user expression), so a wavelength-scale full-wave region hands over to ray tracing for long propagation distances. Rays leave along the outward or inward normal or parallel to the Poynting vector, and can take their frequency from the coupled electromagnetic study.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Release from Electric Field (requires intensity/power computation). API: physics("gop").create("rele1", "ReleaseFromElectricField", 2); feature("rele1").set("E_src", "root.comp1.ewfd.Ex"); set("RayDirectionVector", "OutwardNormal"); set("UseFrequencyCoupledPhysics", "1")

parameters.name: E_src / E
parameters.description: Electric field from a physics interface (must be differentiable) or user defined.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: Parallel to Poynting vector, OutwardNormal (default) or Inward normal.

parameters.name: UseFrequencyCoupledPhysics
parameters.description: Take ray frequency from the Frequency/Wavelength Domain solution.

parameters.name: InitialPosition / Nr
parameters.description: Position method as Release from Boundary (e.g. ProjectedPlaneGrid).

tools.notes: A tangential-field-only source fails; the field must be defined in both tangential and normal directions. Use Parallel to Poynting vector when the outgoing wave is oblique to the release boundary (e.g. next to a PML).

tools.name: Release from Far-Field Radiation Pattern (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: 3D multiscale release that emits rays from grid points with intensity, power and polarization distributed according to a far-field radiation pattern previously computed by a Far-Field Calculation in an RF or Wave Optics model (3D or 2D axisymmetric), so an antenna's radiation can be propagated through electrically huge environments (reflectors, radomes, rooms) by ray tracing. Euler angles reorient the source without recomputing the pattern.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Release from Far-Field Radiation Pattern (RF or Wave Optics license; intensity/power computed). API: physics("gop").create("rffr1", "ReleaseFromFarFieldRadiationPattern", -1); feature("rffr1").set("FarName", "Efar"); set("RayDirectionVector", "Conical"); set("Ealpha", "0[deg]")

parameters.name: GridType / x0
parameters.description: All or Specified combinations of release coordinates.

parameters.name: RayDirectionVector
parameters.description: Spherical (default), Hemispherical or Conical (isotropic cones only); axis from Euler angles or user defined.

parameters.name: FarName
parameters.description: Must match the Far-Field Calculation variable name (default Efar).

parameters.name: Euler angles Ealpha, Ebeta, Egamma (Z-X-Z)
parameters.description: Source orientation.

parameters.name: UseFrequencyFromFarField
parameters.description: Take the ray frequency from the far-field study (monochromatic models).

tools.example:
Dipole antenna pattern from a 2D-axi emw model released as rays in 3D toward a parabolic reflector.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Tutorials/ray_release_from_dipole_antenna_source_3d, ray_release_from_dipole_antenna_source_2daxi
tools.notes: Resolve the near field with about 5 second-order elements per wavelength in the wave model; Expression and Lambertian directions are not allowed because each ray must subtend an equal solid angle.

tools.name: Grating and Diffraction Order (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Boundary feature that treats a surface as a ruled diffraction grating: incident rays release reflected and/or transmitted rays into each diffraction order defined by Diffraction Order subnodes (order m with reflectance and transmittance), using the grating constant, its interpretation on curved surfaces and the direction of periodicity or of grating lines. Orders can be added automatically for a minimum wavelength and angle of incidence, or numbered relative to the blaze angle; optional variables store total transmitted/reflected power.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Grating (default Diffraction Order m = 0). API: physics("gop").create("grat1", "Grating", 1); feature("grat1").set("dg", "1[mm]/600"); set("RaysToRelease", "Reflected"); feature("grat1").create("dfo2", "DiffractionOrder", 1); feature("grat1").feature("dfo2").set("mg", "-1")

parameters.name: dg / InterpretationOfGratingConstant / np
parameters.description: Grating period (default 5 um); UnitCellWidthOnSurface (default) or ProjectedUnitCellWidth with projection direction.

parameters.name: RaysToRelease
parameters.description: ReflectedAndTransmitted (default), Reflected, Transmitted.

parameters.name: UseRelativeOrderNumbers / thetab
parameters.description: Number orders relative to the blaze angle.

parameters.name: DirectionOfPeriodicity / GratingOrientation / Tgp / Tgl
parameters.description: 2D: Forward/Reverse; 3D: user vector or parallel to a reference edge, for periodicity or lines.

parameters.name: Diffraction Order subnode (mg, deltam, Rf, Tr)
parameters.description: Order number, reflectance and transmittance (zero skips the order).

tools.notes: Every extra order consumes secondary rays; size Maximum number of secondary rays accordingly. Order efficiencies can come from an ewfd unit-cell model (Rorder/Torder variables) as in the diffraction_grating verification model.

tools.name: Cross Grating and Diffraction Order (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: 3D boundary feature for two-dimensionally periodic gratings with two grating constants and two (not necessarily orthogonal) directions of periodicity or grating lines; Diffraction Order (Cross Grating) subnodes define order pairs (m, n) with reflectance and transmittance. It models echelle-type cross-dispersers, 2D gratings, diffractive beam splitters and photonic surfaces in ray-traced instruments.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Cross Grating (3D). API: physics("gop").create("xgrat1", "CrossGrating", 2); feature("xgrat1").set("dg1", "sigma_ech"); set("dg2", "sigma_xdp"); set("DirectionOfPeriodicity1", "ParallelToReferenceEdge"); feature("xgrat1").create("xdfo2", "CrossDiffractionOrder", 2)

parameters.name: dg1 / dg2
parameters.description: Grating constants (defaults 1 um and 2 um).

parameters.name: GratingOrientation1/2, DirectionOfPeriodicity1/2, Tgp1/Tgp2, Tgl1/Tgl2
parameters.description: Specify periodicity or lines per direction; direction 2 may be orthogonal to direction 1.

parameters.name: RaysToRelease / StoreTotal...Power
parameters.description: Reflected and/or transmitted; total power variables.

parameters.name: Diffraction Order (mg, ng, Rf, Tr)
parameters.description: Order pair and efficiencies.

tools.notes: Reference edges for the directions must be adjacent to the grating boundaries and not parallel to each other.

tools.name: Linear Polarizer (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Optical device boundary that transmits only the ray polarization component along a transmission axis (user vector, parallel to a reference edge in 3D, or in-plane/out-of-plane in 2D), updating the Stokes parameters through the Mueller matrix of an ideal linear polarizer. Available when ray intensity or power is computed.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Optical Devices > Linear Polarizer. API: physics("gop").create("lpol1", "LinearPolarizer", 2); feature("lpol1").set("TransmissionAxisSpecification", "UserDefined"); set("Ta", new String[]{"1", "0", "0"})

parameters.name: TransmissionAxisSpecification / Ta
parameters.description: UserDefined vector, Parallel to reference edge (3D), In-plane or Out-of-plane (2D).

tools.example:
Crossed polarizers with a wave plate in between: lpol1 Ta = (1,0,0), Linear Wave Retarder, lpol2 Ta = (0,1,0); plot polarization ellipses gop.pax/gop.pbx along the rays.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Tutorials/linear_wave_retarder
tools.notes: An Accumulator (Boundary) subnode is available on all optical-device nodes.

tools.name: Ideal Depolarizer (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Optical device boundary that reinitializes the Stokes parameters so that rays leave completely unpolarized while keeping their intensity, e.g. to represent scrambling optics or to reset polarization after a component whose polarization behavior is not modeled.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Optical Devices > Ideal Depolarizer (intensity or power computed). Type string: IdealDepolarizer.

parameters.name: New Value of Auxiliary Dependent Variables
parameters.description: Optional updates of user auxiliary variables.

tools.example: Fiber-bundle exit face treated as a depolarizer: Ideal Depolarizer on the exit boundary before the imaging optics, so the downstream Fresnel losses use unpolarized light.
tools.notes: See 'Theory of Mueller Matrices and Optical Components' in the Ray Optics User's Guide.

tools.name: Linear Wave Retarder (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Optical device boundary representing an ideal linear retarder (wave plate) with a fast axis and a retardance delta: pi/2 for a quarter-wave plate, pi for a half-wave plate. It transforms the ray polarization through the corresponding Mueller matrix without modeling the crystal.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Optical Devices > Linear Wave Retarder. API: physics("gop").create("lwav1", "LinearWaveRetarder", 2); feature("lwav1").set("FastAxisSpecification", "UserDefined"); set("Fa", new String[]{"1", "1", "0"}); set("deltal", "pi/2")

parameters.name: FastAxisSpecification / Fa
parameters.description: User defined vector, Parallel to reference edge (3D), In-plane/Out-of-plane (2D).

parameters.name: Retardance deltal
parameters.description: Phase retardation in rad.

tools.notes: Requires intensity or power computation.

tools.name: Circular Wave Retarder (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Optical device boundary that rotates the polarization ellipse by a retardance (an ideal optical rotator, e.g. an optically active or Faraday element). By default a positive retardance always means clockwise rotation; optionally the sense depends on the direction in which the ray crosses the boundary, with a Reverse option.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Optical Devices > Circular Wave Retarder. Type string: CircularWaveRetarder.

parameters.name: Retardance delta
parameters.description: Rotation in rad.

parameters.name: Sense of rotation depends on ray trajectory / Reverse sense of rotation
parameters.description: Direction-dependent (nonreciprocal-like) behavior relative to the displayed normal.

tools.example: Optical isolator sketch: Linear Polarizer, Circular Wave Retarder (delta = pi/4, direction dependent), second polarizer at 45 deg; back-reflected rays are blocked.
tools.notes: Requires intensity or power computation.

tools.name: Mueller Matrix (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: General optical device boundary that applies a user-defined 4x4 Mueller matrix (isotropic, diagonal, symmetric or full) to the Stokes vector of each ray, relative to a reference axis. It represents any linear polarization element - partial polarizers, retarders with loss, measured component data - that is not covered by the dedicated devices.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Optical Devices > Mueller Matrix. Type string: MuellerMatrix.

parameters.name: Reference axis specification
parameters.description: User defined (R), Parallel to reference edge (3D), In-plane or Out-of-plane (2D).

parameters.name: Mueller matrix M
parameters.description: Isotropic, Diagonal, Symmetric or Full entries (may depend on ray wavelength).

tools.example: Partial polarizer with 90 % / 10 % transmission: Mueller Matrix with M = 0.5*[[1.0, 0.8, 0, 0],[0.8, 1.0, 0, 0],[0, 0, 0.6, 0],[0, 0, 0, 0.6]].
tools.notes: The matrix acts on the Stokes parameters gop.s0..s3; physical matrices must not amplify the degree of polarization beyond 1.

tools.name: Fluence Rate Calculation (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Domain feature that computes the fluence rate - the total radiant power incident on a small sphere per unit cross-sectional area - on the mesh from the power of the rays crossing each element, as an accumulated variable <gop>.<feature>.E0 (for example gop.frc1.E0). It is the dose-relevant quantity for UV disinfection, photochemistry and photodynamic therapy.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Fluence Rate Calculation (ray power computed). API: physics("gop").create("frc1", "FluenceRateCalculation", 3)

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Domains where the fluence rate is accumulated (element-wise).

tools.notes: Resolution depends on both mesh size and number of rays; 'Only store accumulated variables' keeps the file small for millions of rays.

tools.name: Deposited Ray Power, Domain and Boundary (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Accumulator-type features that convert ray power into heat sources: Deposited Ray Power (Domain) computes the volumetric source from attenuation of rays in absorbing media (variable such as gop.dsrc1.Qsrc), and the Deposited Ray Power subnode of Wall computes the incident energy flux on a surface (variable such as gop.wall1.bsrc1.Qp), optionally smoothed over a radius. The results feed heat transfer boundary or domain heat sources in solar receivers, laser targets and detectors.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Deposited Ray Power; right-click Wall > Deposited Ray Power (ray power computed). API: physics("gop").feature("wall1").create("bsrc1", "DepositedRayPowerBoundary", 2); physics("gop").create("dsrc1", "DepositedRayPower", 3)

parameters.name: ComputeSmoothedAccumulatedVariable / rsm
parameters.description: Average within a sphere of the smoothing radius (boundary version).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Absorbing domains, or the parent wall's boundaries.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gop").feature("wall1").create("bsrc1", "DepositedRayPowerBoundary", 2);
// Heat Transfer > Boundary Heat Source with Qb = gop.wall1.bsrc1.Qp on the receiver; Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Applications/solar_dish_receiver_designer
tools.notes: For fully coupled ray heating in domains use the Ray Heat Source multiphysics coupling; the deposited power variables are accumulated (discontinuous) fields on the mesh.

tools.name: Accumulator, Domain and Boundary (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Features that define mesh-element degrees of freedom accumulated from rays. Accumulator (Domain) sums a source expression R over the rays in each element (or integrates it over time as rays pass), and Accumulator (Boundary), a subnode of Wall, Material Discontinuity, gratings and optical devices, increments on every ray-wall interaction or counts rays that stop on each element. With Density the value is divided by element volume/area (e.g. irradiance from gop.Q), with Count it is not; results may be restricted to one release feature and smoothed.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Accumulator; right-click Wall > Accumulator. API: physics("gop").feature("wall1").create("bacc1", "BoundaryAccumulator", 2); feature("wall1").feature("bacc1").set("AccumulatorType", "Density"); set("R", "gop.Q"); set("AccumulatedVariableName", "rpb"); set("DependentVariableQuantity", "heatflux")

parameters.name: AccumulatorType
parameters.description: Density (default) or Count.

parameters.name: AccumulateOver
parameters.description: Domain: Elements or Elements and time (source interpolation Constant/Linear/Quadratic/Exponential); Boundary: RayWallInteractions (default) or RaysInBoundaryElements.

parameters.name: AccumulatedVariableName / R
parameters.description: Default rpd (domain) or rpb (boundary), e.g. gop.wall1.bacc1.rpb; source expression.

parameters.name: ReleaseFeature / Units / Smoothing
parameters.description: All or one release feature; unit of the variable; smoothing radius rsm.

tools.example:
Irradiance map on a receiver: Wall (Freeze) > Accumulator (Boundary), Density, R = gop.Q, unit W/m^2; a second accumulator with Count and R = 1 counts hits per element.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Applications/solar_dish_receiver_designer
tools.notes: Accumulated variables use discontinuous shape functions; enable smoothing for nicer plots. Domain type string is DomainAccumulator (from the Ray Optics plugin); boundary type BoundaryAccumulator.

tools.name: Nonlocal Accumulator (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Subnode of Release from Boundary that sends information from where rays currently are back to the boundary element that released them, e.g. to compute view factors, the fraction of emitted power reaching a target, or per-element transmission maps of a source surface. The source expression can be collected from active rays in domains, from rays frozen or stuck on boundaries, or both, as a density or count, instantaneous or integrated over time.
tools.usage: Right-click Release from Boundary > Nonlocal Accumulator. Type string: NonlocalAccumulator.

parameters.name: Accumulator type / Accumulate over
parameters.description: Density or Count; Elements or Elements and time.

parameters.name: Accumulated variable name / Source R
parameters.description: Default name rpi.

parameters.name: Source geometric entity level
parameters.description: Domains, Boundaries, or Domains and boundaries.

parameters.name: Smoothing
parameters.description: Radius default 0.1 m.

tools.example: LED package extraction efficiency per emitter element: Release from Boundary on the die, Nonlocal Accumulator with R = gop.Q*(z > z_top) over Boundaries, then plot the accumulated variable on the die surface.
tools.notes: Works only for rays released by the parent feature.

tools.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Global feature that adds a user-defined ODE to every ray, integrated with respect to time or along the ray trajectory with a source expression R; walls, discontinuities and grating orders can reset or increment it. Use it to track custom per-ray quantities such as a diffraction-order index, geometric path length, time spent in a region or accumulated absorption.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Auxiliary Dependent Variable. API: physics("gop").create("aux1", "AuxiliaryField", -1); feature("aux1").set("fieldVariableName", "m"); set("R", "0"); set("Integrate", "WithRespectToTime")

parameters.name: fieldVariableName
parameters.description: Default rp; must not clash with position/wave-vector names.

parameters.name: Source R
parameters.description: Right-hand side of the ODE.

parameters.name: Integrate
parameters.description: WithRespectToTime or along the ray trajectory (R = 1 gives path length).

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: Dependent variable quantity or custom unit.

tools.example:
Track the diffraction order in a Rowland spectrometer: aux variable m with R = 0; in each Diffraction Order subnode set the new value of m for reflected rays to the order number.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Tutorials/rowland_circle_spectrometer
tools.notes: Initial values are set in each release feature (distribution options available); 'Initialize before wave vector' allows directions to depend on it.

tools.name: Ray Continuity (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Pair condition that lets rays cross identity-pair boundaries of an assembly geometry (Form Assembly) as if they were not there, since the meshes on the two sides need not match. It is added by default to the Geometrical Optics interface; with Form Union it is usually unnecessary.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Pairs > Ray Continuity (default instance dpcon1, type PairContinuity).

parameters.name: Pair Selection
parameters.description: Identity pairs whose source and destination overlap.

tools.example: Lens and mount imported as separate objects and finalized with Form Assembly (so each part can be meshed independently): the identity pairs between the air regions get the default Ray Continuity 1, so rays pass through the pair boundaries unaffected.
tools.notes: Positions do not jump across the pair, so source and destination must coincide geometrically.

tools.name: Ray Detector (Geometrical Optics)
tools.description: Domain or boundary feature that reports which rays (from all or one release feature) reach its selection: number of transmitted rays gop.rd1.Nsel, transmission probability gop.rd1.alpha, the logical inclusion expression gop.rd1.rL for filtering Ray Trajectories plots, and the total transmitted power when ray power is computed. It does not change the solution, so it can be added afterwards and evaluated with Study > Update Solution.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains or Boundaries > Ray Detector. Type string: RayDetector.

parameters.name: Release feature
parameters.description: All (default) or a specific release feature.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Detector domains or boundaries.

tools.example: Stray-light path analysis: add Ray Detector rd1 on the sensor, then Ray Trajectories > Filter with expression gop.rd1.rL to show only rays that reach it; Global Evaluation of gop.rd1.alpha gives the fraction.
tools.notes: Right-click Study > Update Solution to evaluate new detector variables without re-solving.

tools.name: Ray Variables: Intensity, Power, Stokes Parameters, Phase and Optical Path (gop.I, gop.Q, gop.L)
tools.description: Per-ray variables of the Geometrical Optics interface available in Ray Trajectories, Ray plots and Ray Evaluation: ray position qx, qy, qz and wave vector kx, ky, kz, intensity gop.I, power gop.Q (initial values gop.I0, gop.Q0), Stokes parameters gop.s0..gop.s3, phase gop.Psi (with Compute phase), optical path length gop.L, reflection count gop.Nrefl, vacuum wavelength gop.lambda0, principal wavefront radii gop.r1, gop.r2, polarization-ellipse axes gop.pax..paz and gop.pbx..pbz, and refractive index on rays gop.nref (domain variable gop.nref_local, spectral-line indices gop.nrefd/nrefF/nrefC and Abbe number gop.Vd).
tools.usage: Ray Trajectories > Color Expression gop.I; Ray plot of gop.Q versus t; Ray Evaluation of gop.L; Volume plot of gop.nrefd.

parameters.name: gop.I / gop.Q
parameters.description: Intensity (W/m^2) and power (W), depending on the intensity-computation option.

parameters.name: gop.s0 ... gop.s3
parameters.description: Stokes parameters (s0 relates to intensity).

parameters.name: gop.L / gop.Nrefl
parameters.description: Optical path length and number of reflections (if enabled).

parameters.name: gop.pax..paz, gop.pbx..pbz
parameters.description: Semi-major and semi-minor axes of the polarization ellipse.

parameters.name: gop.nref / gop.nref_local / gop.nrefd / gop.Vd
parameters.description: Ray and domain refractive index, d-line index, Abbe number.

tools.example:
Polarization ellipses along rays crossing a wave plate: Ray Trajectories with an Arrow/ellipse rendering based on gop.pax, gop.pay, gop.paz and gop.pbx, gop.pby, gop.pbz.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Tutorials/linear_wave_retarder, Ray_Optics_Module/Prisms_and_Coatings/achromatic_phase_shifter (gop.pax)
tools.notes: Ray variables exist only on rays; evaluate domain quantities with *_local variables. Phase is valid only with 'Compute phase' and assumes infinite coherence length.

tools.name: Ray Statistics and Global Variables (gop.pidx, gop.Nt, gop.rrms)
tools.description: Built-in bookkeeping variables of the Geometrical Optics interface: ray index gop.pidx, release feature index gop.prf, release time gop.prt; with Store ray status data also gop.rti (release time incl. secondary rays), gop.st (stop time) and gop.fs (final status 0 unreleased, 1 active, 2 frozen, 3 stuck, 4 disappeared) plus fractions gop.fac, gop.fds, gop.ffr, gop.fst, gop.fse and secondary-ray counts. Global variables give the total ray count gop.Nt, rays in a dataset selection gop.Nsel, transmission probability gop.alpha and per-release counts such as gop.relg1.Ntf; spot statistics include the average position gop.qavex, relative positions gop.deltaqx, RMS spot size gop.rrms (or gop.relg1.rrms per release) and gop.rmaxall.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation of gop.rrms at the focal plane time or on an Intersection Point dataset; Ray Trajectories filter with gop.prf == 2; Ray Evaluation of gop.fs.

parameters.name: gop.pidx / gop.prf / gop.prt
parameters.description: Per-ray index, release feature number, release time.

parameters.name: gop.rti / gop.st / gop.fs
parameters.description: Status data (Store ray status data).

parameters.name: gop.Nt / gop.Nsel / gop.alpha / gop.<release>.Ntf
parameters.description: Global ray counts and transmission probability.

parameters.name: gop.qavex..z / gop.deltaqx..z / gop.rrms / gop.rmaxall
parameters.description: Average and relative ray positions, RMS and maximum spot radius (physics or feature scope).

tools.example:
Focus search: Global plot of gop.relg1.rrms versus time in a Ray Tracing study with path-length steps; the minimum gives the best-focus distance.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/alvarez_lens (gop.rrms), petzval_lens_optimization (gop.relg1.rrms as objective), Ray_Optics_Module/Solar_Radiation/vdara_caustic_surface (status data)
tools.notes: Fractions count unreleased secondary rays in the denominator (e.g. gop.fac = active/(primary + allocated secondary)).

tools.name: Nonlocal Couplings over Rays (gop.sum, gop.ave, gop.max, gop.min)
tools.description: Operators that reduce an expression over rays: gop.sum(expr), gop.ave(expr), gop.max(expr), gop.min(expr) over active, frozen and stuck rays, the _all variants (gop.sum_all, gop.ave_all, gop.max_all, gop.min_all) over every ray including unreleased and disappeared ones (which may give NaN), and two-argument forms such as gop.max(gop.I, qx) that evaluate a second expression on the ray where the first is extreme. They are used for total transmitted power, average path length, peak intensity location and optimization objectives.
tools.usage: Any global expression, e.g. Global Evaluation of gop.sum(gop.Q) or gop.ave(gop.L); older names gop.gopop1, gop.gopaveop1, gop.gopmaxop1 are deprecated aliases.

parameters.name: gop.sum(a) / gop.sum_all(a)
parameters.description: Sum over rays (sum_all(isnan(qx)) counts unreleased and disappeared rays).

parameters.name: gop.ave(a) / gop.ave_all(a)
parameters.description: Arithmetic mean.

parameters.name: gop.max(a) / gop.min(a) (+ _all)
parameters.description: Extremes; NaN handling may be platform dependent for _all.

parameters.name: gop.max(a,b) / gop.min(a,b)
parameters.description: Value of b on the ray where a is maximum/minimum.

tools.example:
Total power reaching the receiver: gop.sum(gop.Q*(gop.fs==2)) at the last time step; position of the brightest ray: gop.max(gop.I, qx).
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Tutorials/plane_em_wave_to_ray_release (gop.sum), Ray_Optics_Module/Laser_Cavities/bow_tie_laser_cavity (deprecated gop.gopop1 form)
tools.notes: Evaluate at a specific solution time; the operators act on the ray dataset of that time.
